title: The Campaign of Khaybar (Muḥarram 7 AH)
app_target: 3D Seerah learning app for ages 12-25 (interactive 3D scenes; battle timeline; verse overlays)

spine_source.work: Raheeq al-Makhtum (MSA NIU English ed.), Saifur Rahman al-Mubarakpuri, trans. Issam Diab (Dar-us-Salam)
spine_source.khaybar_chapter_pages: UNLOCATED — task 1.1 of the build-khaybar change; locate in the owned PDF before grading
spine_source.citation_format: Raheeq al-Makhtum (MSA NIU English ed.), p. N

skeleton_note: Entries below are DRAFT claims from general seerah knowledge, written to seed grading work. NONE is graded. Every entry must pass live verification (sunnah.com HTML pages + api.alquran.cloud) and spine-page confirmation before its grade is set; no choreography may key to any entry before the owner reviews the graded ledger (build-khaybar task 1.5).

conventions.block_tagging: Same as badr.json: all entries HISTORY; no reflections in this phase.
conventions.honorifics: The Prophet is referenced as 'the Prophet (PBUH)' in rendered text; Companions carry honorifics at first mention per block. No figural depiction of the Prophet (PBUH) or any face.
conventions.quote_cap: Direct on-screen quotes <= 15 words; Quran fetched live from api.alquran.cloud at build time.
conventions.no_harmonization: DISPUTED entries display ranges/both versions, never merged. UNKNOWN = not yet verifiable this session; hidden by default.
conventions.secondary_sirah: Ibn Hisham/Ibn Ishaq-derived claims are cited via Raheeq or online reproductions logged in live_verification_log.

grading_policy.CERTAIN: >= 2 independent sources, at least one canonical (Quran > Sahih Bukhari/Muslim > other canonical collections > sirah Ibn Hisham/Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Sa'd, al-Tabari > modern critical works). Raheeq al-Makhtum alone never certifies.
grading_policy.REPORTED: Solid single-chain sirah/hadith detail; accurate to attribute but from one lineage or modern retelling only; rendered with no certainty implied.
grading_policy.DISPUTED: Transmitted variants conflict; app must show ranges/both versions, never harmonized.
grading_policy.UNKNOWN: Cannot be verified from owned + live sources; never rendered without user approval.

render_as_policy.solid: Canonical or >=2 independent sources; safe as primary on-screen facts, may carry direct quotes.
render_as_policy.approx: Reported or contested detail; render visually/ambiguously, quotes flagged, no Fame-of-truth framing.
render_as_policy.hidden: Do not render in current phase; visible only in an app 'scholar's mode' if the user approves.

entries.claim: DRAFT — After al-Ḥudaybiyyah (6 AH), the Prophet (PBUH) marched north on Khaybar in Muḥarram 7 AH: a fortified Jewish oasis whose leaders had mustered confederates against Madinah at the Trench.
entries.notes: Core context beat; expected CERTAIN after spine + one canonical cross-check. Verify the month (Muḥarram 7 AH) explicitly.

entries.claim: DRAFT — The Muslim force is commonly reported at about 1,400 men with around 100-200 horses; specific figures vary by narration.

sources.work: proposed: sunnah.com search for the 1,400 narration (ʿUmar listing)

variants.note: The '1,400' figure appears in hadith wordings whose Khaybar attachment must be verified; other counts circulate in sīrah.

entries.notes: Crowd-count source for the scene. Do not render any total until graded; if DISPUTED, show the range.

entries.claim: DRAFT — Khaybar lies roughly 90-140 km north of Madinah in volcanic ḥarra terrain: black rock uplands over an oasis of palm groves and fields, forts built on high ground.
entries.notes: Terrain brief for the heightfield. Distance band needs fresh live checks like BADR-017.

entries.claim: DRAFT — Khaybar was a chain of fortresses; name-sets in circulation include al-Naʿīm, al-Qamūṣ, al-Shaqq, Naṭāh, al-Katībah, al-Waṭīḥ and al-Sulālim.

variants.note: Fort name-sets and their spellings differ across sīrah sources; expected DISPUTED after grading.

entries.notes: Scene shows a small number of distinct forts; label only the forts the graded set supports.

entries.claim: DRAFT — The order in which the forts fell differs by report; the app must stage a range, never one confident order.

variants.note: Expected to become DISPUTED once the spine and one more source are compared (e.g., Naʿīm-first vs Qamūṣ-last orderings).

entries.notes: Direct input to choreography task 3.2. Do not harmonize.

entries.claim: DRAFT — The campaign is commonly reported at about one month overall, with the al-Qamūṣ siege sometimes given at 10-14 days.
entries.notes: Affects phase pacing labels; keep durations off-screen unless graded.

entries.claim: DRAFT — The army arrived at Khaybar by night and engagement opened in the morning; associated sayings of that night/morning exist in the collections and must be verified verbatim before any use.
entries.notes: Phase 2 (march/night arrival) hinge. No on-screen text until verified.

entries.claim: DRAFT — The forts were taken one by one in sequence rather than in a single assault.
entries.notes: Underpins the sequential-siege choreography; expected uncontroversial but must be graded.

entries.claim: DRAFT — The Prophet (PBUH) said he would give the banner 'tomorrow' to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger and whom Allah and His Messenger love, and gave it to ʿAlī (RA).

sources.work: proposed: Sahih al-Bukhari (Sahl b. Saʿd chain) — locate exact number

variants.note: ʿAlī's accompanying vow wording ('fight until they believe') needs separate verification.

entries.notes: The standard-grant beat. Expected CERTAIN after the Bukhari number is confirmed; the vow may grade separately.

entries.claim: DRAFT — ʿAlī (RA) had an eye ailment at Khaybar before receiving the banner; details are sīrah-level.
entries.notes: Humanizing detail; keep out of render unless graded at least REPORTED; no depiction of the affliction beyond a label.

entries.claim: DRAFT — Marḥab, a Khaybar champion, came out in armour and boasted in verse; ʿAlī (RA) met him in single combat and killed him.

sources.work: proposed: locate any canonical parallel (sunnah.com search 'Marhab')

variants.note: The boast poetry wording varies by chain; the named pair and the kill are the stable core.

entries.notes: Signature duel beat (build-khaybar task 3.4). No dialogue on screen beyond what a solid/report grade supports; never render the boast verbatim unless graded.

entries.claim: DRAFT — After Marḥab fell, his brother Yāsir engaged ʿAlī (RA) and was killed.
entries.notes: Optional second beat inside the duel phase; stage only if graded.

entries.claim: DRAFT — Al-Qamūṣ, the chief fortress, fell after a siege; reports differ on the manner of its fall. A report of a Jewess dropping a millstone on a Muslim at the fort circulates.

variants.note: Fall-manner variants expected DISPUTED; millstone report single-lineage.

entries.notes: The siege phase's climax; stage the siege, keep the fall manner per graded variants.

entries.claim: DRAFT — A Khaybar shepherd tending the flocks asked about Islam, accepted it, and joined the army; the flocks are reported to have followed without being driven.
entries.notes: Candidate vignette; the flocks detail is the part to grade carefully before staging animals.

entries.claim: DRAFT — The Khaybar people were allowed to remain and farm, yielding half the produce to the Muslims — the first fayʾ.

sources.work: proposed: Sahih al-Bukhari (Ibn ʿUmar narration) — locate exact number

entries.notes: Reckoning phase backbone; expected CERTAIN after verification.

entries.claim: DRAFT — Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy (RA) was among those captured, was freed, and her freedom became her dowry; the Prophet (PBUH) married her.

sources.work: proposed: Sahih al-Bukhari / Sahih Muslim (Ṣafiyyah narrations) — locate exact numbers

entries.notes: Rendered as a label beat only; no depiction issues arise since no face is shown anywhere.

entries.claim: DRAFT — A Jewish woman roasted a sheep and poisoned it; Bishr b. al-Barāʾ (RA) ate and died (timing varies by report); the Prophet (PBUH) spat saying the shoulder had told him it was poisoned; the woman confessed.

sources.work: proposed: Sahih al-Bukhari + Sahih Muslim parallel — locate exact numbers

variants.note: Name of the woman (Zaynab bint al-Ḥārith) and Bishr's death timing vary; grade the core event and the names separately.

entries.notes: Sober-history beat for the reckoning; parental-guidance framing like BADR-056.

entries.claim: DRAFT — Fadak came to terms without fighting, offering half its produce.
entries.notes: One-line map beat only; keep out of the 3D scene unless the owner wants it.

entries.claim: DRAFT — Jaʿfar b. Abī Ṭālib (RA) returned from Abyssinia around the time of Khaybar's conquest; the Prophet (PBUH) said he could not tell which gladened him more.

sources.work: proposed: sīrah chain + any canonical parallel — verify wording

entries.notes: Warm closing beat; wording must be verified verbatim before any quote.

entries.claim: DRAFT — Sūrah al-Fatḥ's context (the Ḥudaybiyyah aftermath) is linked by mufassirin to the clear gain at Khaybar; 48:20-21's 'much booty' is tied to Khaybar by some exegeses.

sources.work: proposed: tafsir + live fetch of 48:20/21 en.sahih

variants.note: Verse-to-battle attribution is exegetical, not explicit; render as bridge only if the owner accepts the framing.
